title: Consumer life is becoming a verification and attention-management problem as choice, convenience, personalization, and AI compound
source_unit: Kearney Consumer Institute, The Tyranny of Too Much: Global Future Consumer Study 2026
geography: Consumers across 20 countries spanning the Americas, Europe, Middle East and Africa, and Asia Pacific

observations.period: May 2026 survey; future consumer study frame

denominator.unit: consumers surveyed across 20 countries; gender and income census representation, with younger consumers in the majority

study_focus.value: trust, time, social connection, product discovery, social media, financial security, and technology

compounding_effect.value: choice, convenience, personalization, inputs, tasks, and interactions can transfer more verification and coordination work onto consumers

future_horizon.unit: year used for the report's forward-looking consumer scenario

observations.method: Kearney Consumer Institute global consumer survey across 20 countries, with forward-looking interpretation and scenario framing; the release reports a younger-skewed sample and census-appropriate gender and income representation.
observations.uncertainty: The study is a commercial foresight exercise with a younger-skewed sample; its 2036 claims are scenarios and strategic interpretations, not forecasts or observed population change.
observations.subgroup: Consumers across 20 countries, especially Gen Z and Millennials, plus consumers navigating financial security, digital discovery, social media, and AI-mediated decisions.
observations.counterinterpretation: More choice and personalization can increase agency and convenience for some consumers; the burden may be reduced by good interfaces, trusted intermediaries, regulation, or shared household and community support.

contestable_spending.unit: trillion US dollars of consumer spending the report estimates could become contestable through trust failures and brand switching by 2036

outcome_over_brand.unit: percent agreeing they care more about whether something works than about the brand

trust_shift.value: trust is described as shifting from source-based trust in institutions, experts, media, and brands toward outcome- and performance-based trust

verification_load.value: consumers must increasingly assess which claims are real, which products work, and which agents can help decide

observations.method: Survey evidence and Kearney scenario interpretation; the $20 trillion figure is a forward-looking estimate rather than measured switching or lost sales.
observations.uncertainty: Brand switching, trust failure, and contestable-spending estimates depend on assumptions about behavior, category boundaries, income, and future information environments.
observations.subgroup: Consumers evaluating brands, platforms, product claims, influencers, agents, and sources in high-information environments.
observations.counterinterpretation: Performance-based trust can reward better products and accountability, but it may also privilege short-term measurable outcomes over provenance, ethics, identity, or long-term reliability.

free_time_change.unit: minutes of additional free time the report projects consumers may get from AI and automation

time_reabsorption.value: freed time may be reabsorbed or redirected into more tasks, monitoring, comparison, and interaction

time_model.value: time shifts from chronological scarcity toward contextual allocation across multitasking, discovery, media, rest, and connection

observations.method: Forward-looking Kearney consumer scenario based on survey responses and strategic interpretation; no time-use diary or longitudinal automation measurement is reported in the release.
observations.uncertainty: The projected minutes are not a causal estimate of AI productivity or household time; automation may redistribute tasks rather than reduce total cognitive load.
observations.subgroup: Consumers with different levels of digital access, care work, employment flexibility, financial security, and ability to delegate tasks to technology.
observations.counterinterpretation: Automation can create genuine room for rest, care, creativity, or sociality when institutions and interfaces protect that room instead of filling it with new demands.

observations.period: 2036 scenario; synthetic social connection and human empathy

human_empathy_preference.unit: percent believing only people, not technology, can provide genuine empathy and belonging

ai_accuracy_ceiling.unit: percent reported as the peak accuracy in synthetic testing within the study's discussion

synthetic_connection.value: greater AI use may change how people allocate attention and seek connection, including emotionally charged interactions

social_tradeoff.value: consumers may delegate emotional questions to AI while still expecting human connection to remain non-replicable

observations.method: Kearney survey and qualitative/scenario interpretation as reported in the public release; the accuracy figure is retained as source context without independent reconstruction of the synthetic test.
observations.uncertainty: The study does not establish how AI emotional use changes wellbeing, relationships, loneliness, trust, or social inequality; stated preference may not predict future behavior.
observations.subgroup: Consumers using AI for advice, discovery, emotional interaction, companionship, or social coordination, with unequal access to human support.
observations.counterinterpretation: AI-mediated interaction may supplement human connection for some people, especially where human support is scarce, while creating risks of misdirection, dependency, or reduced accountability.

related_sources.claim: IKEA Life at Home 2026 provides complementary evidence on household control, comfort, security, and climate action.
WEF technology foresight provides complementary evidence on AI, trust, access, and distributed systems.
Edelman Trust Barometer provides complementary institutional, intergroup, and consumer trust evidence.

boundary: This record adds a forward-looking consumer route linking choice overload, verification work, performance-based trust, AI-mediated time, attention, and synthetic social connection. It is a Kearney commercial survey and foresight scenario, not a causal experiment, longitudinal time-use study, representative age distribution, clinical assessment, or realized 2036 forecast.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The public Kearney release on PR Newswire was reviewed for sample, countries, study timing, demographic framing, trust, time, AI, social-connection, spending, and scenario claims; the full report was not publicly downloadable from the release.
